mutations.name: trailingIpv4 reads words 4/5 instead of 6/7 — the extracted 'embedded v4' becomes 0.0.0.0, so NAT64 (both prefixes) and v4-compatible ::a.b.c.d are reported as NOT private and reach image.js's fetch. This was the real bug: the first version of the fix had it, and the failure was silent
NAT64 local-use prefix branch removed — 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215) stops recursing on its embedded v4, so 64:ff9b:1::7f00:1 reads as public
6to4 branch removed — 2002::/16 stops recursing, so 2002:7f00:1::1 (carries 127.0.0.1) reads as public
Teredo branch removed — 2001:0::/32 stops recursing on the one's-complemented client v4
OVER-BLOCK CONTROL — the v4-compatible recurse fires for ::0.0.0.0 too, i.e. the guard starts treating the unspecified address as embedded-private

_known_redundancy: v4CompatibleToHexGroups is dead code: measured 2026-09-13, with trailingIpv4 reading the right words (6/7), expandIpv6 already parses '::127.0.0.1' correctly, so both call sites of the helper are no-ops and removing them changes no answer for any tested input. It is left in place because the removal edit is where this file was broken twice; deleting it is a follow-up with its own test run, not a rider on this fix.
_not_covered: No mutation pins the v4-compatible normalisation call site because no mutation of it can be caught — that is what 'redundant' means here. The carrier prefixes (NAT64 local-use, 6to4, Teredo) and the trailingIpv4 word choice ARE pinned.
